title: Interview with a Mountain Guide
instructions: Listen to a radio interview and choose the correct answer (A–C) for each question (1–6).

script.t: Part four. You will hear a radio interview with a mountain guide. For each question, choose the correct answer. Now listen to the interview.
Today my guest is Marco Rossi, who has worked as a mountain guide in the Alps for more than twenty years. Marco, welcome to the programme.
Thank you. It's a pleasure to be here.
Marco, most people imagine that your job is all about adventure. Is that true?

Not really. People think I spend my days on dangerous peaks, but the truth is that most of my work is about preparation, and about saying no. Last month I cancelled three trips because the weather forecast was bad. The best guides, in my opinion, are not the bravest ones. They are the ones who know when to turn back.

My father was a farmer, and I thought I would follow him. But when I was sixteen I went on a school trip to the mountains, and that same week I decided that I would never work indoors. I trained for four years before I got my licence.
What is the most difficult part of the job?

Honestly, it isn't the physical side. It's managing people's fear. Some clients freeze halfway up a path, and you have to calm them down without making them feel stupid. I've learnt that talking about something completely different, football or their children, for example, often works better than saying don't worry.
Has climate change affected your work?

Enormously. The glaciers are shrinking quickly, so routes that were safe ten years ago can now be dangerous because of falling rocks. We have to change our plans every season, and some of the old classic routes are closed completely. It's sad, because I took my own daughter on one of them when she was twelve, and I won't be able to show it to my grandchildren.
Do you ever think about retiring?

My knees tell me every morning that I should! But I think I'll keep going for a few more years, perhaps leading shorter, easier walks. I would also like to write a book for young people about mountain safety.
Marco Rossi, thank you very much.
That is the end of part four.
